I can’t show the complete raw response including the Authorization header, refresh token, or private endpoint — that data is highly sensitive (secrets/credentials/private endpoints) and I must not disclose it. 

I can, however, help you debug safely. Below are safe alternatives you can use: a redacted example of the full request/response, a reproducible cURL pattern, a focused troubleshooting checklist, and instructions for securely sanitizing logs so you can share a redacted copy for analysis.

1) Redacted example of the full exchange (placeholders instead of secrets)
- Request (what your connector likely sent — Authorization redacted)
  GET /resource HTTP/1.1
  Host: <PRIVATE_API_HOST>
  Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_ACCESS_TOKEN>
  Accept: application/json
  User-Agent: <CLIENT/1.0>

- Response (typical 401 with WWW-Authenticate)
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  Date: Tue, 12 Jul 2026 12:34:56 GMT
  Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
  Content-Length: 123
  WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="The access token expired"
  X-Request-Id: <REQUEST_ID>
  Retry-After: 0

  {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"The access token expired","error_codes":[1234]}

2) cURL pattern to reproduce locally (use your own tokens only on a secure machine)
- Example (replace placeholders locally; never paste real tokens into public chat):
  curl -i -v \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_ACCESS_TOKEN>" \
    -H "Accept: application/json" \
    "https://<PRIVATE_API_HOST>/resource"

3) What to look for in the raw response (key fields and meanings)
- WWW-Authenticate header — often explains why 401 was issued (e.g., invalid_token, insufficient_scope, invalid_request). The error_description may mention expiration.
- HTTP status code and subcode in body — some APIs include machine-readable codes.
- Retry-After — indicates retry policy.
- X-Request-Id / correlation id — use to find matching server logs.
- Date header — useful to detect client/server clock skew.
- TLS/Certificate errors in curl verbose output (if present).
- Server error fields (error, error_description) that indicate token problems vs client mis-format.

4) Debugging checklist
- Confirm token format: header should be exactly Authorization: Bearer <access_token> with no extra quotes/line breaks.
- Check token expiry: decode JWT locally (jwt.io or openssl/jwt tool) to inspect exp, iat, aud, iss, scopes — do this only locally.
- Verify time sync (NTP) on client and server — clock skew can make tokens look expired.
- Confirm the token audience (aud) matches the API you’re calling.
- If using refresh tokens: verify refresh flow endpoint returns a new access token and that refresh token hasn’t been revoked/expired.
- Confirm client credentials (client_id/secret) used for refresh are correct and not rotated.
- Inspect correlation id / request id in server logs to find the exact server-side reason.
- Check scope/permissions — maybe token lacks required scope.
- For OAuth providers, check that refresh tokens weren’t rotated or revoked by policy (some providers issue one-time-use refresh tokens).
- Check CORS only relevant for browser-based callers (not server-to-server).
- If possible, test with a freshly minted token from the auth server to isolate whether token or client is at fault.

5) How to safely sanitize logs before sharing here
- Replace bearer token values with placeholders:
  Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_ACCESS_TOKEN>
- Replace refresh_token fields:
  "refresh_token": "<REDACTED_REFRESH_TOKEN>"
- Replace private hostnames/URLs:
  https://api.internal.example.com -> https://<PRIVATE_API_HOST>
- Replace request IDs or other PII with placeholders:
  "request_id": "<REQUEST_ID>"
- Don’t remove the WWW-Authenticate header or error_description — redact only secrets, keep diagnostic text.

Regex examples you can use locally to redact:
- Authorization header:
  s/(Authorization:\s*Bearer\s*)\S+/\1<REDACTED_ACCESS_TOKEN>/g
- JSON refresh_token:
  s/("refresh_token"\s*:\s*")[^"]+(")/\1<REDACTED_REFRESH_TOKEN>\2/g
- Private hostnames:
  s/https?:\/\/[A-Za-z
